feedback: The confession follows the available chain: Hugh knew the uncanceled purchase condition, had a serious refund-exposure motive, visited the unattended glass, and supplied the false substitution story. It confirms the inferred extraction and transfer rather than introducing a new decisive clue. His closing concern with becoming impossible to remember gives emotional shape to his earlier fear of losing respectability. The explanation of which documents contradicted him is somewhat instructional and could be shorter once players have voted. Brie's staff-centered response and Chip's failed protective instinct give the other suspects credible aftermaths. I find the reveal earned, though the absence of a uniquely identifying physical transfer keeps the solution dependent on recognizing Hugh's particular source-denial lie.
